source.title: The neural computational and dynamical mechanisms of reward-modulated spatial coding in hippocampal place cells.

confidence_rationale: Directly on-target as a computational existence proof that reward-location over-representation and its dynamic shift can be generated by a simple reward-distance-dependent modulation -- SD-024's phenomenon, reproduced in silico. But it is mixed rather than supporting because the mechanism it uses is a dynamic GAIN on existing units in a continuous attractor network, which is exactly the alternative SD-024's weight-independent density discriminator is designed to rule out. It is simultaneously the best available proof-of-concept and the sharpest statement of the confound.
failure_signatures: Over-representation and its shift to a relocated reward were reproduced without any change in the number or placement of representational units -- a distance-dependent gain on a fixed attractor population sufficed. Any REE measurement that reads density off activity or weights will therefore not discriminate SD-024's allocation mechanism from a gain mechanism.

The model is not fit to or validated against recorded data; it reproduces a qualitative phenomenon in 1D tracks and 2D square arenas. Its 5-10 cm over-representation zone is a model output, not a measured constraint, and should not be imported as a scale for da_jitter_radius.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Two continuous-attractor place-cell sub-models (position-integrated and velocity-driven) with a reward-location-dependent dynamic gain, modulated by Euclidean distance between the animal and the reward, reproduce both place-field over-representation within 5-10 cm of reward zones and the shift of maximum field density when the reward is moved.
mapping.ree_translation: Establishes that SD-024's target phenomenon -- concentrated representational resource at reward locations, tracking the reward when it moves -- is computationally cheap and does not require environmental richness. That is SD-024's central bet (a workaround for the ARC-057 substrate constraint) and this paper supports it. It simultaneously identifies the discriminating question REE must answer experimentally: is the density in the residue field structural (more centers) or apparent (more gain on the same centers)?
mapping.mapping_caveat: A continuous attractor network with distance-dependent gain is not an RBF field with FIFO center allocation. The two architectures agree on the phenomenon and disagree on the mechanism, so this paper cannot be counted as support for SD-024's implementational commitment -- and read strictly it is a live competing explanation. This is the reason SD-024's compute_local_density is weight-independent, and the reason MECH-232 (which SD-024 was built to test) is still candidate.
mapping.source_context: Simulation only; 1D linear track and 2D square environment; no animal data, no parameter fitting to recordings.

confidence_components.notes: Modest venue and a purely simulated, unfitted model, so source quality is capped. Mapping fidelity is genuinely two-sided: high on the phenomenon, low on the mechanism. Transfer risk is low precisely because it is already a computational model -- there is no species or modality gap, only an architectural one.
